observation_summary: The StringUtils.join method throws a NullPointerException when an element in the input array returns null from its toString() method, because the code assumes that calling toString() on an array element will always return a non-null string to calculate the initial capacity of the StringBuilder.
reasoning_summary: The root cause is a missing validation of the result of the toString() call. The code attempts to calculate the initial capacity of a StringBuilder by calling toString() on an array element (array[startIndex].toString().length()). If that element's toString() returns null, the subsequent .length() call triggers a NullPointerException. This is a classic case of missing validation of data (the result of the toString() call) before using it in a way that assumes non-nullity.
evidence_used: The bug report states: 'StringUtils.join throws NPE when toString returns null for one of objects in collection'

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the capacity calculation is part of an algorithm, the failure is specifically due to the lack of a check on the result of the toString() method, which is a validation issue.
